messages.content:
The issue occurs in the `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.cpio.CpioArchiveInputStream` class in the `getNextCPIOEntry()` method. The method reads the magic bytes of the CPIO entry and based on the magic bytes, it determines the type of CPIO entry to read (old binary, new, old ASCII). 

The issue seems to be related to the handling of the magic bytes of the CPIO entry. If the magic bytes do not match any of the expected values, an `IOException` is thrown with the message "Unknown magic [magicString]". This indicates that the magic bytes in the CPIO archive being read do not match any of the expected values, leading to an unexpected EOF (End of File) exception during the unpacking process.

To resolve this issue, the code logic for handling unknown magic bytes should be improved to either handle the case gracefully or provide more specific information about the encountered magic bytes to aid in debugging the issue.

Next, I will suggest the methods that should be fixed to address this issue.
The following methods should be fixed to address the unexpected EOF issue in the CPIO archive unpacking:
- `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.cpio.CpioArchiveInputStream.getNextCPIOEntry()`
- `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.cpio.CpioArchiveInputStream.readFully(byte[], int, int)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
